extraction.reason: Not recorded when the page was cached, and not recovered since. What the .txt shows is a tag-stripping of the .html rather than a browser rendering: it keeps the site navigation chrome, decodes entities, holds each paragraph on one line, and carries artefacts only a regex stripper leaves - a bare `--->` where a comment opened with a `>` inside it, and a fragment of a meta attribute ending `">`. Two candidates were run on 2026-09-09 and NEITHER reproduces extractedTextSha256: a regex stripper (tags to newlines, entities decoded, blank lines dropped) and Chromium's document.body.innerText through Playwright. This is not cosmetic: content/levels/ottawa.json cites this digest as the sourceHash of its territory statement, so a shipped claim is pinned to bytes that only a machine already holding the file can produce. Someone who fetched the page and matched its sha256 still cannot check the quote.

knownStaleness.topic: A dated news release, not a maintained page
knownStaleness.problem: This is a point-in-time release from 5 June 2024, not a page anyone keeps current. It is cited for a statement about territory, which does not expire, but the document around it may be withdrawn or rewritten. The maintained alternative, RCAANC's Algonquins of Ontario land-claim page, states the same two facts in separate sentences: the treaty sentence never names Ottawa, and the Ottawa sentence describes the extent of a claim rather than a Crown finding. Only this release carries both halves in one contiguous string, which is what a quote has to be.

liveChecks.consequence: Fetched first-hand, and the prose is unmoved - but THE REGISTER'S sha256 NO LONGER REPRODUCES. The live fetch is 37,851 bytes hashing to e63d288f50b3ccaf26de7f4e40835ac86bb3970252f30a085a20483bba08b6da against this register's 37,852 bytes and b20dd776919c80fe4478badd0e9806c7f854e05eee722787a8b70c789d8610c2. The whole of the difference is the Akamai BOOMR beacon block at the foot of <head> - request id, edge timestamp, connection port and signature - and nothing else; the python3 tag-stripper recorded verbatim as extraction.command in cirnac-treaty-7.json and kdfn-about-us.json, run over the live fetch and over the cached file, and the two outputs diffed produced an EMPTY diff. So extractedTextSha256 (8276d6ce...), which is the digest content/levels/ottawa.json cites as its sourceHash, still matches, and the finding is that this URL cannot be re-fetched to this register's sha256 by anyone, ever, because that field captured one CDN response rather than the document. That is a defect in what the register pins, not a revision, and it is recorded here rather than fixed because re-hashing would pin the next response just as uselessly. NOTE FOR THE FLAG OWNER, NOT ACTED ON HERE: the release names "the Honourable Gary Anandasangaree, Minister of Crown-Indigenous Relations", and canada.ca today names the Honourable Rebecca Alty in that office. A dated news release will never correct that, which is the textbook upstream: "does-not-revise" case with a bannedFromAnswers list of the minister's name and title - but declaring it would move this chapter to row 2 and silence the volatile demand the contract gate is making on content/levels/ottawa.json right now, so the verifier recorded it and left the declaration to whoever can read the level prose. WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: the single flag here declares upstream "unknown" by omission, so the chapter stays on ADR-0016 section 2 row 1 and the claim's clock is still unarmed.
